_comment_: Operators realm — Phase 13. Imported via `kc.sh start --import-realm` (foundations §8 bootstrap-only; subsequent config drift goes through gocloak Admin API). The realm is intentionally locked down: no self-registration, no password reset, no broker IdPs, no public clients beyond saas-operator-cli (PKCE-only). MFA is enforced via two default required actions (TOTP + WebAuthn). The 5-min step-up window is enforced server-side in internal/platform/auth/operatorjwt/stepup.go — Keycloak emits `auth_time`, the platform decides freshness.
_comment_lifespans_: accessTokenLifespan == 900s (15 min) — matches AGENTS.md §18.4 max impersonation TTL. ssoSessionIdleTimeout 1800s lets short breaks not log the operator out; ssoSessionMaxLifespan 28800s caps a full session at 8h, after which re-auth is required regardless of activity.
_comment_brute_force_: Lock an account after 5 wrong passwords; quick-recover after 1 min on the first failure, max 15 min on repeats. Permanent lockout disabled so an attacker cannot lock out an operator indefinitely from the public auth page; the brute-force counter resets on a successful login.
_comment_required_actions_: Default required actions on every new operator: enroll TOTP AND register a WebAuthn key. Either satisfies the MFA AMR check at the platform side (otp / hwk / webauthn). Operators see both screens on first login.
_comment_password_policy_: 12-char min, mixed case + digit + special, last 12 hashes remembered, max 90-day rotation. argon2id (Keycloak's default since 22.0).
passwordPolicy: length(12) and notUsername(undefined) and notEmail(undefined) and digits(1) and lowerCase(1) and upperCase(1) and specialChars(1) and passwordHistory(12) and forceExpiredPasswordChange(90) and hashAlgorithm(argon2)
_comment_otp_policy_: TOTP, 6 digits, SHA1 (RFC 6238 default; the QR-renderer in authenticator apps is universally compatible), 30s period, 1-step look-behind window.
_comment_webauthn_policy_: WebAuthn policy: any attestation, any authenticator (platform or roaming), require user verification = preferred (no biometric forcing for hardware keys). The relying party id is set at provisioning by the platform admin via gocloak — the placeholder is replaced before MVP.
_comment_acr_loa_map_: Map ACR claims to loa (level of assurance). silver=1 (password only), gold=2 (password + MFA, fresh). Step-up middleware requires gold + auth_time within 5 min for destructive endpoints.
_comment_flows_: browser-with-mfa: copy of the built-in browser flow with a REQUIRED MFA step right after the username+password screen. The exact step is conditional-otp (Keycloak's built-in OTP authenticator that also accepts a registered WebAuthn key when the user has one). Token's `amr` claim ends up containing `pwd` + (`otp` | `hwk`). The 5-min step-up freshness is NOT enforced at Keycloak — see CONVENTIONS / AGENTS.md §18.4 — it is the platform's responsibility because Keycloak does not natively expose 'force re-auth if older than X seconds'.

authenticationFlows.description: Browser flow with required MFA after password (operators realm).
Either OTP or WebAuthn; at least one must be configured.

clients._comment_: Confidential service-account client used by the controlplane Go process to call Keycloak's admin REST (operator listing, role assignments, password resets). The audience-mapper forces aud=saas-control on every issued access token so operator JWTs are unambiguously bound to the control plane — a misrouted token to the data plane fails aud check.
clients.name: SaaS Control Plane Service Account

clients._comment_: saasctl PKCE client. publicClient + PKCE S256 — no client secret in the binary. Callback is the operator's localhost:8765 loopback (RFC 8252). post.logout.redirect.uris=+ allows any of the configured redirectUris on logout.
clients.name: saasctl CLI (PKCE)

protocolMappers._comment_: operator_id is set as a user attribute by the platform at operator-create time; the mapper copies it into the access token as a top-level claim that the verifier reads alongside sub.
protocolMappers.name: operator-id-attribute

_comment_roles_: Realm roles map to OAuth scopes via the role-to-claim mapper. operator-admin is composite — assigning it grants the full destructive surface. The atomic roles let an org separate read-only auditors from incident-response operators.

realm.name: tenants.impersonate
realm.description: Mint operator-impersonation tokens against a Deployment.

realm.name: operator
realm.description: Default role for every operator user — read-only across the control plane.

realm.name: operator_admin
realm.description: Full control plane access; required for impersonation + operator management.

_comment_default_roles_: Every freshly created operator picks up the `operator` (read-only) composite. Promotion to operator_admin is a manual step performed by an existing operator_admin via the saas-controlplane service account.
_comment_users_: Empty by default — the realm import installs no operators. The platform admin creates the first operator via the saas-controlplane service account, which then sends an email invite (verifyEmail flow). All subsequent operators are managed through saasctl operator add (post-MVP) or the gocloak admin path.
_comment_smtp_: SMTP target for verify-email + password-reset (resetPasswordAllowed is false in this realm, but verify-email still uses SMTP). Local dev points at mailhog; production fills in the real SMTP credentials via gocloak post-import.
